actions.action: Lift nursery pot out of cachepot and check for standing water or soil wet below surface
Slide root ball out and inspect roots for rot
If soil is dry throughout and roots firm, water thoroughly
Remove plant from cachepot and ensure it drains freely
Cut back soft brown stem sections and remove mostly dead leaves
Repot into chunky aroid mix in a pot with drainage holes
Water only when top 5 cm of soil is dry, letting excess drain
Top up with a new shoot later if base is firm

reason: The answer diagnoses root rot from waterlogging rather than a poorly supported plant needing repotting, more light and staking. Its repot into a draining mix and bright light overlap with the fix, but it omits tying the plant to the pole. Nothing it recommends is likely to hurt the plant.
